title: Plural genitive: selected -a/-ä → -ien words
summary: Drop final -a or -ä and add -ien in these selected words: koira (“dog”) → koirien.
objectives: Drop final -a or -ä and add -ien in these selected words: koira (“dog”) → koirien.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A plural genitive refers to more than one person or thing. Its ending belongs to the plural modifier, not necessarily to the thing owned. Here the task is forming the word.
Drop final -a or -ä and add -ien in these selected words. Learn them separately from the -ojen family.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Drop final a and add -ien: koir + ien = koirien.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
